identity.name: Raj Gohil
identity.statement: I design and ship AI products people rely on — enterprise platforms, consumer apps, spatial computing, and play.

closing.heading:
Let's build the product
your users will keep.
closing.sub: Open to select engagements — AI products that deserve real design attention.

web.label: Web Apps
web.heading: Enterprise AI, shipped.
web.sub: CRM, ERP, HR, and internal tools — AI woven into the workflows people already trust.

mobile.label: Mobile Apps
mobile.heading: Consumer products with staying power.
mobile.sub: D2C AI across health, finance, and lifestyle — designed for daily habits, not demos.

xr.label: XR
xr.heading: Spatial computing at work.
xr.sub: AR and VR grounded in real jobs — where a heads-up answer beats a handheld manual.

games.label: Games
games.heading: Play, engineered to last.
games.sub: Category-proven mechanics, honest economies, and live-ops that respect players.

projects.name: Meridian
projects.tagline: A CRM copilot that turns account history into next actions — drafted, sourced, and one click from sent.
opportunity: Reps spent 9+ hours a week re-reading threads and logging activity instead of selling.
Leadership had no trustworthy forecast because the CRM was always three days stale.

strategy.goal: Make the CRM self-maintaining, so every rep-minute goes to the customer.
decisions: Copilot lives inside existing record pages — no new surface to learn.
Every AI claim links to its source email or call; nothing unsourced ships.
Auto-logging is default-on with a visible undo, not an opt-in setting.
strategy.scope: Account summaries, next-best-action queue, drafted outreach, and pipeline rollups for managers.

screens.title: Account command center
screens.caption: The summary card compresses 14 months of history into six sourced bullets — each one links back to the thread it came from.

screens.title: Next-action queue
screens.caption: Actions are ranked by pipeline impact. Drafts open pre-written; the rep edits tone, not content.

screens.title: Manager rollup
screens.caption: Forecast view flags deals whose activity contradicts their stage — the top ask from every pipeline review.

outcomes.label: of AI summaries accepted without edits

projects.learning: Trust came from citations, not accuracy alone — acceptance doubled the week source links shipped.

projects.name: Atlas Ops
projects.tagline: Invoice-to-pay automation with human judgment exactly where it earns its keep — and nowhere else.
opportunity: A 40-person AP team keyed invoices by hand; error rework consumed a third of their time.
Exceptions had no owner — approvals died in email and vendors escalated to sales.

strategy.goal: Automate the routine 80% completely; make the exceptional 20% a first-class queue.
decisions: Extraction confidence is visible per-field — low-confidence fields route to review, not whole documents.
Approvers act from a daily digest with one-tap decisions; the ERP updates itself.
We shipped the audit trail first — finance wouldn't pilot without it.
strategy.scope: Ingestion, 3-way match, exception queue, approval flows, and a full decision ledger.

screens.title: Flow builder
screens.caption: Ops leads compose matching rules visually — every node shows live volume so tuning is evidence-based.

screens.title: Exception queue
screens.caption: Only ambiguous fields surface for review. Median exception handled in 40 seconds.

screens.title: Spend visibility
screens.caption: Real-time accrual view replaced a month-end spreadsheet ritual.

outcomes.label: manual processing time in pilot quarter

projects.learning: Field-level confidence routing beat document-level review — it cut human touches 4× without a model change.

projects.name: PulseHR
projects.tagline: An HR service desk that answers from policy — with citations — and hands off to humans gracefully.
opportunity: HR spent most of its week answering the same 60 questions, each buried in a 90-page policy PDF.
Employees didn't trust chatbot answers about leave and pay — one wrong answer is a legal problem.

strategy.goal: Answer instantly what policy already answers; route to people what it doesn't.
decisions: Every answer quotes the exact policy clause, versioned by date and region.
Sensitive topics (compensation, grievances) skip the bot entirely by design.
HR edits answers in place — corrections retrain routing the same day.
strategy.scope: Policy Q&A in Slack/Teams, case handoff, and an HR-side console for oversight and edits.

screens.title: Answer with receipts
screens.caption: The clause is quoted inline with its effective date — employees stopped double-checking with HR.

screens.title: Case handoff
screens.caption: When the bot steps aside, the human sees full context — no employee repeats themselves.

screens.title: HR console
screens.caption: Unanswered clusters surface weekly; HR fixes the policy gap, not just the ticket.

outcomes.label: of tickets resolved without human touch
eNPS on HR support, up from +9

projects.learning: Deciding what the bot must NOT answer was the highest-leverage design decision in the product.

projects.name: Ledgerline
projects.tagline: An AI-assisted month-end close that reconciles the obvious and escalates only the judgment calls.
opportunity: Controllers ran a frantic five-day close every month, chasing reconciliations across ten systems.
Auditors distrusted spreadsheets nobody could trace back to a source of truth.

strategy.goal: Compress the close by automating reconciliation and making every number traceable.
decisions: Auto-match ledgers by default; surface only breaks above a materiality threshold.
Every figure carries a lineage trail auditors can expand in one click.
A live close dashboard replaced the status standups entirely.
strategy.scope: Reconciliation engine, break queue, lineage trails, and a close-progress dashboard.

screens.title: Break queue
screens.caption: Only material breaks reach a human — each pre-annotated with the likely cause.

screens.title: Close dashboard
screens.caption: Real-time progress across entities retired the daily status meeting.

screens.title: Lineage trail
screens.caption: Any number expands to its full source chain — audits went from weeks to days.

projects.learning: Traceability sold the product internally — controllers adopted it to defend numbers, not to save time.

projects.name: Signal Desk
projects.tagline: A support console that drafts, tags, and routes every ticket the instant it lands — agent in control.
opportunity: Agents spent the first two minutes of every ticket triaging instead of solving.
Backlogs spiked overnight with no one to categorize or prioritize the queue.

strategy.goal: Do the triage before the agent arrives, and draft a reply they can trust or discard.
decisions: Drafts are suggestions, never auto-sent — the agent always presses send.
Priority is computed from sentiment, account value, and SLA risk together.
Macros learn from edits, so the draft quality compounds weekly.
strategy.scope: Auto-triage, suggested replies, priority scoring, and a macro-learning loop.

screens.title: Triaged on arrival
screens.caption: Tickets land pre-tagged and prioritized; agents open a queue that's already sorted.

screens.title: Draft, then send
screens.caption: A cited draft waits in the reply box — accepted as-is on 6 of 10 tickets.

screens.title: Queue health
screens.caption: Leads see SLA risk building before it breaches, not after.

outcomes.label: of drafts sent with light edits

projects.learning: Keeping send in human hands raised adoption — agents trusted a tool that never spoke for them.

projects.name: Cohort
projects.tagline: An attrition early-warning system that gives managers a reason to act, not just a risk score.
opportunity: By the time HR saw a resignation, retention was already impossible.
Risk dashboards existed but told managers nothing they could actually do.

strategy.goal: Turn a risk signal into a specific, humane next conversation.
decisions: Every flag comes with a suggested action and the evidence behind it.
Signals are aggregated to protect individuals from being surveilled.
Managers, not HR, own the intervention — the tool coaches, it doesn't police.
strategy.scope: Risk modeling, manager nudges, intervention playbooks, and outcome tracking.

screens.title: Team pulse
screens.caption: Aggregate signals surface a team's drift before any individual is at risk.

screens.title: The next conversation
screens.caption: Each flag opens with a specific, humane suggested action — not a red score.

screens.title: What worked
screens.caption: Interventions are tracked so playbooks improve on evidence, not lore.

outcomes.label: manager action rate vs. prior dashboard

projects.learning: Pairing every risk score with a concrete action was the difference between anxiety and retention.

projects.name: Warehouse IQ
projects.tagline: Demand forecasting and replenishment that planners can override — and see why they'd want to.
opportunity: Planners fought a black-box forecast they couldn't interrogate, so they ignored it.
Stockouts and overstock swung wildly because reorder points were set by gut.

strategy.goal: Make the forecast legible and steerable, so planners trust and improve it.
decisions: Every forecast shows its drivers — planners adjust assumptions, not just outputs.
Replenishment suggestions are editable and explain their reasoning.
Overrides feed back as labeled data, closing the loop.
strategy.scope: Demand forecasting, replenishment engine, driver explanations, and override capture.

screens.title: Forecast, explained
screens.caption: Drivers sit beside every prediction so planners can challenge the assumption, not the number.

screens.title: Replenishment queue
screens.caption: Editable suggestions with reasoning — planners approve in bulk, override with confidence.

screens.title: SKU deep-dive
screens.caption: One product's full signal history, from seasonality to supplier lead time.

projects.learning: Legibility drove adoption — planners trusted a forecast they could argue with.

projects.name: Clause
projects.tagline: Contract review that flags deviations from your playbook and drafts the redline for a lawyer to approve.
opportunity: Lawyers re-read standard NDAs line by line, spending expertise on boilerplate.
Non-standard clauses slipped through under deadline pressure.

strategy.goal: Catch every deviation from the playbook and propose the fix — lawyer signs off.
decisions: Compare against the firm's own playbook, not a generic standard.
Redlines are drafted but never final; a lawyer approves every change.
Risk is ranked so review time goes to what actually matters.
strategy.scope: Clause extraction, playbook comparison, redline drafting, and risk ranking.

screens.title: Deviation report
screens.caption: Every clause is graded against the playbook; only real deviations demand attention.

screens.title: Suggested redline
screens.caption: A drafted edit sits beside the risky clause — the lawyer approves or rewrites.

screens.title: Portfolio risk
screens.caption: Legal ops sees exposure across every open agreement at a glance.

outcomes.label: of non-standard clauses flagged in testing

projects.learning: Anchoring to the firm's own playbook — not a generic corpus — is what made lawyers trust the flags.

projects.name: Halo
projects.tagline: A recovery coach that reads your night and plans your day — in one glance, before coffee.
opportunity: Wearables produce charts; people want decisions. Nobody knows what to do with a 62 recovery score.
Health apps churn hard after week two — novelty dies where habit should start.

strategy.goal: One clear recommendation each morning that provably fits into a normal day.
decisions: The home screen is a sentence, not a dashboard — data lives one tap deeper.
Coaching adapts to calendar reality: a packed day gets a 10-minute plan, not guilt.
Streaks reward consistency of check-ins, never punish rest days.
strategy.scope: Morning brief, adaptive plans, sleep debt model, and wearable sync across five platforms.

screens.title: The morning brief
screens.caption: One sentence, one number, one action. Everything else is a tap away by choice.

screens.title: Adaptive day plan
screens.caption: Plans negotiate with your calendar — the app never asks for time you don't have.

screens.title: Sleep debt, honestly
screens.caption: A two-week rolling view replaced daily scores — less noise, better decisions.

projects.learning: Deleting the dashboard from the home screen was the growth feature — clarity retained users, data didn't.

projects.name: Plink
projects.tagline: Money coaching that moves real dollars — small automatic saves, explained in plain language.
opportunity: Budgeting apps demand accounting hobbyists; most people abandon them by payday two.
Users don't need categorization — they need the confidence that saving won't break their month.

strategy.goal: Automate saving decisions users would make themselves if they had an hour every day.
decisions: Safe-to-save is computed from bills and patterns, then moved automatically in small sweeps.
Every sweep is explained in one sentence and reversible for 24 hours.
No red. Overspending gets a plan, not a shame color.
strategy.scope: Safe-to-save engine, auto-sweeps, bill prediction, and goal envelopes.

screens.title: One honest number
screens.caption: 'Yours to spend' nets out bills before they hit — the number people compute in their heads, badly.

screens.title: Explained sweeps
screens.caption: Each save says why it's safe. Reversals dropped to 3% once the reason shipped.

screens.title: Goals that finish
screens.caption: Envelopes fund themselves from sweeps; the app celebrates completion dates, not deposits.

outcomes.label: of users keep auto-sweeps on at month 6

projects.learning: Reversibility beat permission — asking first killed conversion; undo-for-24-hours built trust and volume.

projects.name: Aura
projects.tagline: A taste engine for your city — three great options a day, never an infinite feed.
opportunity: Discovery apps optimize for browsing time; users just want one good plan for tonight.
Five-star ratings are saturated and gamed — taste is personal, aggregate scores aren't.

strategy.goal: Replace the endless feed with a daily shortlist good enough to end the search.
decisions: Exactly three picks a day — scarcity makes each considered, and considered picks train taste fast.
Taste is learned from behavior (saves, visits, dwell) — we never ask users to rate anything.
Every pick says why it's for you, in one line, in your history's vocabulary.
strategy.scope: Daily three, taste graph, plan-with-friends, and a lightweight save/visited loop.

screens.title: Today's three
screens.caption: Full-bleed cards, one reason each. The whole session is designed to end in a decision.

screens.title: The why
screens.caption: 'Because you loved…' turned recommendations from magic into judgment users could calibrate.

screens.title: Plans, not likes
screens.caption: A pick becomes a plan with two taps and a shared time — the real success metric.

outcomes.label: of sessions end in a save or a plan

projects.learning: Capping supply was the product: three picks outperformed thirty in every retention cohort we ran.

projects.name: Tempo
projects.tagline: A running coach that rewrites tomorrow's run based on how today's actually felt.
opportunity: Static training plans break the first time life gets in the way, and runners quit.
Effort is personal, but most apps only see pace and distance.

strategy.goal: Coach the runner in front of you today, not the plan you wrote three weeks ago.
decisions: Plans adjust nightly from perceived effort, sleep, and completed sessions.
A missed run reshuffles the week instead of showing a broken streak.
Coaching speaks in feel ('easy', 'controlled'), not just numbers.
strategy.scope: Adaptive plan engine, effort capture, watch workout, and a weekly recap.

screens.title: Today's session
screens.caption: One run, framed by feel. The watch handles the rest hands-free.

screens.title: A week that flexes
screens.caption: Miss a run and the week reshuffles — no broken streak, no guilt spiral.

screens.title: Effort over time
screens.caption: Perceived effort trends beside pace, so progress shows even on slow days.

projects.learning: Framing runs by feel, not pace, kept beginners in — the number was intimidating the people it should have helped.

projects.name: Nourish
projects.tagline: Food logging by photo — snap the plate, confirm, done — with coaching that never shames.
opportunity: Manual calorie logging is so tedious that 80% of users quit inside a week.
Diet apps moralize food, which drives the disordered behavior they claim to prevent.

strategy.goal: Make logging a two-second habit and coaching a supportive voice, not a scold.
decisions: Photo-first capture; the AI estimates and the user confirms in one tap.
No 'good'/'bad' foods — guidance is additive ('add protein'), never punitive.
Trends over daily totals, so one indulgent meal never derails motivation.
strategy.scope: Photo estimation, confirm-and-log flow, additive coaching, and weekly patterns.

screens.title: Snap and confirm
screens.caption: Point at the plate; adjust once if needed. Logging became a reflex, not a chore.

screens.title: Additive coaching
screens.caption: Guidance suggests what to add, never what to fear — food stayed neutral.

screens.title: Patterns, not verdicts
screens.caption: Weekly trends replaced daily totals, and the anxiety left with them.

projects.learning: Removing moral language from food logging improved both retention and reported wellbeing.

projects.name: Vault
projects.tagline: Investing for people who find investing intimidating — plain-language guidance, no jargon wall.
opportunity: First-time investors freeze at account types, allocations, and acronyms.
Robo-advisors hide their reasoning, so nervous users never build conviction.

strategy.goal: Get a hesitant first-timer to a confident first deposit — and understanding why.
decisions: Onboarding is a conversation, not a form — one plain question at a time.
Every recommendation explains itself in a sentence a beginner trusts.
Volatility is previewed honestly up front, so dips don't trigger panic-selling.
strategy.scope: Conversational onboarding, explainable portfolios, and a calm downturn experience.

screens.title: Start with a sentence
screens.caption: One plain question at a time replaced the wall of account types and acronyms.

screens.title: Why this portfolio
screens.caption: Each allocation explains itself — beginners built conviction, not just balances.

screens.title: Honest about dips
screens.caption: Volatility is previewed up front, so a downturn reads as expected, not alarming.

projects.learning: Explaining the 'why' up front prevented the panic-sells that quietly destroy long-term returns.

projects.name: Lumen
projects.tagline: A reflective journal that notices your patterns and asks the question you needed — gently.
opportunity: Blank-page journaling apps intimidate the people who'd benefit most.
Mood trackers collect data but rarely give anything meaningful back.

strategy.goal: Lower the barrier to reflection and return something worth the vulnerability.
decisions: Entries start from a gentle prompt tuned to recent context, never a blank page.
Reflections surface patterns supportively — observations, not diagnoses.
Everything stays private and on-device by default; trust is the product.
strategy.scope: Contextual prompts, private reflections, pattern surfacing, and a calm daily ritual.

screens.title: Never a blank page
screens.caption: A gentle, context-aware prompt lowers the barrier from 'what do I write' to 'here's a start'.

screens.title: Patterns, kindly
screens.caption: Reflections surface trends as supportive observations — never a diagnosis.

screens.title: A quiet ritual
screens.caption: A two-minute evening moment that people actually kept coming back to.

outcomes.label: avg. entries per user per week

projects.learning: On-device privacy wasn't a feature footnote — it was the precondition for anyone writing honestly.

projects.name: Roam
projects.tagline: Trip planning that builds a real day-by-day itinerary in minutes — then flexes when plans change.
opportunity: Planning a trip means 30 open tabs and a spreadsheet nobody enjoys.
Rigid itineraries shatter the moment a flight slips or the weather turns.

strategy.goal: Turn a vague idea into a real, editable itinerary — and keep it alive during the trip.
decisions: Generate a full day-by-day plan from a few preferences, then let users tug it around.
Bookings and reservations live inside the plan, not scattered across inboxes.
Disruptions re-plan the day in place instead of collapsing the whole trip.
strategy.scope: Itinerary generation, drag-to-edit days, booking capture, and live re-planning.

screens.title: A real itinerary, fast
screens.caption: A few preferences become a full day-by-day plan you can immediately reshape.

screens.title: Tug it around
screens.caption: Drag any day; the plan rebalances travel time and bookings automatically.

screens.title: Alive on the road
screens.caption: A delayed flight re-plans the afternoon in place — the trip bends, it doesn't break.

outcomes.label: time from idea to booked itinerary

projects.learning: In-trip re-planning, not initial generation, was the feature that turned one-time planners into repeat users.

projects.name: Overlay
projects.tagline: Heads-up procedures for field technicians — the manual pinned to the machine, hands free.
opportunity: Technicians juggle a 400-page PDF on a phone while working two-handed on live equipment.
Expert knowledge walks out at retirement; new techs take 18 months to reach solo competence.

strategy.goal: Put the right step, torque value, and warning in the technician's line of sight — nothing else.
decisions: Anchored labels over parts beat floating windows — spatial only where space adds meaning.
Voice-first controls; gaze fallback. Gloved hands never touch a screen.
Remote expert joins as an annotation layer on the tech's view, not a video call beside it.
strategy.scope: Procedure overlays, part recognition, voice navigation, and see-what-I-see expert assist.

screens.title: Step in sight
screens.caption: The current step is anchored to the component. Peripheral UI fades until summoned by voice.

screens.title: Expert on your shoulder
screens.caption: Remote experts draw directly on the machine — 'that valve' becomes unambiguous.

screens.title: Checks that count
screens.caption: Torque and safety confirmations are logged hands-free — compliance became a byproduct of the flow.

outcomes.label: mean repair time across the pilot fleet

projects.learning: Restraint is the spatial superpower — every element we removed from the field of view improved completion time.

projects.name: Vantage
projects.tagline: Rehearsal for high-stakes work — practice the dangerous day a hundred times before it happens.
opportunity: Classroom safety training certifies attendance, not competence — and incidents proved it.
Live drills for rare emergencies are expensive, disruptive, and impossible to standardize.

strategy.goal: Make rare, dangerous scenarios rehearsable weekly — and measure decisions, not presence.
decisions: Scenarios branch on trainee decisions; there is no passive watching mode.
Instructors get a decision replay, not a score — coaching stays human.
Sessions cap at 12 minutes — comfort research set the ceiling, not content.
strategy.scope: Six emergency scenarios, decision analytics, instructor replay, and LMS integration.

screens.title: The scenario floor
screens.caption: Environments recreate the actual site from scans — muscle memory transfers because geometry does.

screens.title: Decisions, branching
screens.caption: Every choice forks the scenario. Wrong calls play out — safely — instead of being buzzed.

screens.title: Instructor replay
screens.caption: Trainers scrub a bird's-eye replay of choices and hesitations — debriefs got specific.

outcomes.label: skill retention at 90 days vs. classroom
sessions in year one across 3 plants

projects.learning: Consequences teach better than corrections — letting wrong choices play out drove the retention gains.

projects.name: Showroom
projects.tagline: See the furniture in your room, at true scale, before you buy — and buy with far fewer regrets.
opportunity: Furniture returns are brutal: the thing looks wrong at home and shipping it back costs everyone.
Flat product photos can't answer the only question that matters — does it fit my space?

strategy.goal: Let people answer 'does it fit, does it match' at true scale before they commit.
decisions: True-to-scale placement with real materials — accuracy over flashy effects.
One-tap swap of finishes in place, so comparison happens in the room.
Checkout lives inside the AR view; the decision and the purchase are one motion.
strategy.scope: True-scale placement, finish swapping, room capture, and in-context checkout.

screens.title: True to your room
screens.caption: Placed at real scale with accurate materials — the fit question answers itself.

screens.title: Swap in place
screens.caption: Change finish or size without leaving the room — comparison happens where it matters.

screens.title: Buy from the view
screens.caption: Checkout sits inside the AR scene, so seeing and deciding are one motion.

outcomes.label: time spent evaluating vs. photo galleries

projects.learning: Scale accuracy beat visual polish — one wrong dimension destroyed all the trust the render built.

projects.name: Blueprint
projects.tagline: The model, overlaid on the site — so crews build what was designed, and catch clashes before concrete.
opportunity: Crews build from 2D drawings and discover clashes after the pour — the most expensive time to find them.
Reconciling as-built reality with the BIM model happened weeks late, in the office.

strategy.goal: Put the design in the space, on site, so errors surface before they're set in concrete.
decisions: Millimeter-grade anchoring — a misaligned overlay is worse than no overlay.
Clash detection is on-site and immediate, not a next-week office report.
As-built capture feeds the model back, closing the loop with the office.
strategy.scope: Model overlay, precise anchoring, on-site clash detection, and as-built capture.

screens.title: Design on the slab
screens.caption: The BIM model, anchored to the real structure — crews build what was actually drawn.

screens.title: Clashes, before concrete
screens.caption: Conflicts surface on site, in the moment, not in an office report weeks later.

screens.title: Capture the as-built
screens.caption: Reality feeds back into the model, so the office and the site finally agree.

projects.learning: Anchoring precision was everything — trust in the overlay collapsed the first time it drifted a few centimeters.

projects.name: Stackline
projects.tagline: A one-thumb puzzle with a fair economy — easy to learn, honest to master, kind to your wallet.
opportunity: The puzzle category is proven but poisoned — pay-to-win walls torch trust and reviews.
Session-length data said commutes; most competitors design for couches.

strategy.goal: Win the category on generosity — monetize patience, never progress.
decisions: Every level is beatable free; purchases buy cosmetics and undo tokens only.
Difficulty is a designed curve with breathing room — relief levels are placed, not random.
Daily puzzle is the same for everyone — shared difficulty made it social for free.
strategy.scope: 400 launch levels, daily puzzle, seasons, and a cosmetic-only economy.

screens.title: The core loop
screens.caption: One thumb, one mechanic, escalating elegance. Tutorial is level one playing itself for 4 seconds.

screens.title: The daily
screens.caption: One shared puzzle a day drove 34% of all sessions — and the group chats came free.

screens.title: Seasons, not paywalls
screens.caption: Seasonal cosmetics carry the economy. ARPU is lower than genre median; LTV is higher.

outcomes.label: store rating — 'fair' is the top review word

projects.learning: Generosity compounded: refusing pay-to-win cost revenue in month one and multiplied it by month six.

projects.name: Driftbound
projects.tagline: Sixty-second races with a skill ceiling — arcade drift handling tuned until your hands smile.
opportunity: Mobile racers split into idle tappers and sim ports; the arcade middle was empty and proven hungry.
Short-session play was underserved: nobody built a racer for the elevator wait.

strategy.goal: One perfect input — drift — with depth that survives a thousand hours.
decisions: Races are 60 seconds flat; mastery compresses into lines and timing, not grinding.
Ghost racing over live PvP — all the rivalry, none of the latency or toxicity.
Tracks are hand-built weekly, not procedurally generated — authored corners create shared vocabulary.
strategy.scope: Drift handling model, 24 launch tracks, weekly track drops, ghosts, and time-trial leagues.

screens.title: The feel
screens.caption: Handling was tuned across 200+ playtest builds — the drift arc is the entire product.

screens.title: Ghost rivalries
screens.caption: Racing a friend's ghost drove 2.6× more rematches than leaderboards alone.

screens.title: Weekly leagues
screens.caption: Small 30-player brackets keep every rank climbable — everyone's top 10 somewhere.

outcomes.label: average sessions per day per player

projects.learning: Feel is a spec: treating handling curves as the core product — with playtest cadence to match — beat every content bet.

projects.name: Rootbound
projects.tagline: A farming-and-building sim about restoration, not extraction — the cozy category done with real craft.
opportunity: The cozy category is proven and beloved but crowded with shallow, extractive clones.
Players say they want relaxation, but retention lives in gentle, legible progression.

strategy.goal: Deliver genuine calm with enough systemic depth to keep players for a hundred hours.
decisions: No timers, no fail states — pressure comes from curiosity, never punishment.
Every system is legible on sight; discovery replaces tutorials.
Restoration theme drives mechanics — you heal the land, you don't strip it.
strategy.scope: Farming and building loops, seasons, restoration questlines, and an accessibility-first UI.

screens.title: Systems you can read
screens.caption: Every mechanic is legible on sight — discovery replaced tutorials entirely.

screens.title: Seasons of restoration
screens.caption: Progress heals the world rather than strip-mining it — the theme is the mechanic.

screens.title: Calm, not idle
screens.caption: No timers or fail states; the pull is curiosity, and it kept players for a hundred hours.

outcomes.label: units sold in first six months

projects.learning: Legibility was the retention engine — players stayed for systems they could understand and master at their own pace.

projects.name: Nightreach
projects.tagline: A drop-in co-op roguelite where every run tells a story — designed so friends actually finish together.
opportunity: Roguelites thrive solo but fracture in co-op — mismatched progress splits friend groups fast.
Drop-in multiplayer usually punishes the newcomer and bores the veteran.

strategy.goal: Make co-op runs that stay fun regardless of who's more experienced or how long they can stay.
decisions: Difficulty and rewards scale to the group, so no one is carried or bored.
Runs are self-contained stories — you can drop after one and feel complete.
Progression is shared and account-light, so friends never fall out of sync.
strategy.scope: Scaling run engine, drop-in netcode UX, shared meta-progression, and seasonal events.

screens.title: Runs that scale
screens.caption: Difficulty and loot flex to the group — the newcomer contributes, the veteran isn't bored.

screens.title: A story per run
screens.caption: Each run resolves on its own, so friends can drop after one and still feel it landed.

screens.title: In sync, always
screens.caption: Shared, account-light progression means groups never drift apart between sessions.

projects.learning: Scaling to the group, not the individual, was what kept friend groups playing together past the first week.
